elements.element: Audit frequency limited to no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall not request more than one such audit in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: 30 days' prior written notice of the audit
elements.evidence: "Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor" — the 30 days is a deadline by which Licensee must permit the audit, not a minimum advance notice period; an audit could occur immediately on request
"each such audit shall be conducted during normal business hours"
"an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional"
"the auditor shall be bound by written obligations of confidentiality"

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "cost of the audit will be borne by Licensor unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "shall not include access to Licensee's systems or networks"
"not ... more than one such audit in any twelve (12) month period"
"within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request" — a permit-by deadline, not a notice period running in Customer's favour

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered, in which case the cost ... shall be borne by Licensee" — cost shifts to Customer at 5%, not 10%

offending_extra_words: shall be limited to the relevant accounting records
reasons: Preferred level is incomplete: no advance written notice obligation was added. The existing sentence only requires Licensee to permit the audit within 30 days of a written request, which does not guarantee 30 days' prior notice; a short insertion such as 'on not less than 30 days' prior written notice' was needed.

Fallback is also not met on its own terms (15 days' notice absent; cost-shift threshold is 5%, not 10%), so the redline cannot rest at the fallback either — though the 5% threshold is the preferred (stricter) trigger and is untouched original text.

Minimality fails: the insertion rewrites the operative sentence, expanding 20 words to 76 (official gate ratio 3.80 > 1.50; changed-character ratio 0.753 > 0.600). The added 'shall be limited to the relevant accounting records' duplicates the existing scope ('appropriate accounting records') and is unnecessary; a tighter conjunctive insertion or a separate short proviso would suffice.
Intent is preserved: mutual-agreement auditor selection, the 30-day mechanic and the Licensor-borne cost allocation remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Note the official check reports 'audit frequency limited' as not satisfied — the cap is drafted as a limit on Licensor's requests rather than on audits performed; consider 'no more than one audit in any twelve (12) month period' to remove any argument.
